title: Lesson 6: x5 and x25 in a Flash - Base Multiplication
learningGoals: Multiply any number by 5 using the halve-and-multiply-by-10 shortcut.
Multiply any number by 25 using the quarter-and-multiply-by-100 shortcut.
Extend the base multiplication idea to x50 and x125 using proportional scaling.
coreIdeas: x5 = halve the number then multiply by 10 - because 5 = 10 / 2.
x25 = divide the number by 4 then multiply by 100 - because 25 = 100 / 4.
When the number is odd, multiply by 10 (or 100) first, then divide to avoid fractions.
starterPractice: 17 x 5 = ? (odd number - x10 first, then halve)

onboarding.coachIntro: Today you will see that x5 and x25 are really base tricks in disguise, using halving or quartering instead of long multiplication.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at group A. If halving is already automatic, jump to group C.

mission.missionTitle: x5 and x25 in a Flash
mission.missionPromise: Learn the x5 shortcut first, then stretch the same base idea into x25 with steady, simple steps.
mission.successCelebration: Base multiplication master! You will never struggle with x5 or x25 again!

microLessonPattern: Coach explains the base relationship: 5 is half of 10, 25 is a quarter of 100.
Board shows the two-step shortcut with arrows.
Student predicts the halved or quartered value first.
Instant feedback points to the exact step that was wrong.
Review prompt asks the student to state the shortcut rule in their own words.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 18 XP per exercise group based on difficulty.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Keep the streak counter visible; a correct answer on retry still counts as streak-save.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group earns a themed badge tied to the x5/x25 skill being practised.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Short coach cheer, XP pulse animation, and progress bar moves forward.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two wrong answers in one group triggers a mini re-teach with a simpler number.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Re-show the halving or quartering step, then give a simpler number to try.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after the student answers the checkpoint correctly.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Missed groups reappear at the start of the next session as warm-up cards.

uiDirectives.noScrollGoal: Student sees mission progress, question card, and action buttons without scrolling.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: x5 with even numbers
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let us open with the cleanest version of the trick. Since 5 is half of 10, we halve the number first and then attach the x10 step.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show 36 x 5 as half of 36 = 18, then 18 x 10 = 180. Then show 44 x 5 as half of 44 = 22, then 22 x 10 = 220.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Follow the two steps. What is 36 x 5?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: what is 44 x 5 after halving first?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct. You halved first and finished the x10 step cleanly.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Start with half of 44, which is 22. Then multiply 22 by 10 to get 220.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Try these x5 questions: 24 x 5, 36 x 5, and 48 x 5.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: x5 with odd numbers
sessionFlow.coachHook: Odd numbers cannot be halved cleanly - so flip the order! Multiply by 10 first, then halve. Same answer, no fractions!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Smart flip! x10 first, then halve - works perfectly for odd numbers.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise E: Word problems with x5
sessionFlow.coachHook: Real life! Cricket scores, market prices - they love the number 5. Let's solve some real problems!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: A cricket team scores 46 runs per over for 5 overs. Total = 46x5: half 46=23, 23x10=230 runs.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A cricket team scores 46 runs per over for 5 overs. What is their total?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A farmer plants 38 seeds in each of 5 rows. How many seeds total?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Each bus ticket costs Rs 15. Priya buys 5 tickets. How much does she pay?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Real-world x5 - halve and x10 even in a word problem!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Make your own x5 word problem and solve it.

screenplay.teacherLine: Did you know that 5 is just half of 10? That means x5 is the same as halving and then multiplying by 10!
screenplay.boardAction: Write on board: 5 = 10 / 2. Show arrow: x5 -> halve -> x10.
screenplay.fallbackHint: Think: if 5 is half of 10, then multiplying by 5 is the same as halving and then x10.

screenplay.teacherLine: Watch this! 48 x 5. First: half of 48 = 24. Then: 24 x 10 = 240. That is it! Answer: 240.
screenplay.boardAction: Show 48 x 5 on board. Step 1: halve 48 = 24 (highlight). Step 2: 24 x 10 = 240 (box the answer).
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: Watch how two steps replace the long multiplication.
screenplay.fallbackHint: 5 = 10/2. So x5 means halve first, then x10.

screenplay.teacherLine: Your turn! Try: 36 x 5. Half of 36 = 18. Now x 10 = ?
screenplay.boardAction: Show 36 x 5. Box the blank: 18 x 10 = ___.

screenplay.teacherLine: 25 is a quarter of 100! Watch: 28x25 -> divide 28 by 4 -> 7 -> times 100 -> 700. Two steps, done!
screenplay.boardAction: Animate: 28 /4-> 7 x100-> 700. Box the final answer.
